report.summary: Both failures are the same Page.goto timeout on /books, and the app was up (the fixture waited on /health), so this is not an infrastructure outage. The likely cause is the seeded slow_list bug in app/main.py, which adds a random 0-8 s delay to book listing and can exceed the 5 s timeout. Start by confirming whether BUGS=slow_list is set in the CI environment, and fix the app's listing delay (or stop enabling it in CI) before touching the tests.

causes.title: /books sometimes takes longer than the 5 s navigation timeout because list_books injects a random 0-8 s delay
causes.explanation: GET /books renders through render_books(), which calls list_books(). When the slow_list bug is enabled, list_books sleeps for a uniform random 0-8 s before querying. The fail_fast fixture sets the Playwright default timeout to 5000 ms, and page.goto waits for the 'load' event, so any sleep above roughly 5 s makes goto time out. Roughly 3/8 of calls should exceed the limit, so the outcome depends on chance and the same code can pass on a rerun. Other tests that open /books with the same fixture passed in this run, which fits intermittent slowness rather than a consistent failure. The root cause is the timing-dependent app behavior, not the test code. Note that the app's worst case (8 s) is larger than the test's 5 s budget, so the test can never be made reliable against it without changing one side.
evidence: Call log for both tests: 'navigating to "http://127.0.0.1:59814/books", waiting until "load"' and 'Timeout 5000ms exceeded.' (ports 59814 and 59812, different workers).
app/main.py:12 and :6-13 docstring: 'slow_list  random 0-8 s delay when listing books (flaky timing)'.
app/main.py:264-270: render_books() calls list_books(user["id"]) on every GET /books.
tests/ui/conftest.py:4-7: autouse fail_fast fixture sets page.set_default_timeout(5000), with the docstring 'Nothing in this app should take longer than 5 s'.
tests/conftest.py:31-42: _wait_until_up() polls /health before the tests run, so the server was up and the failure is not a startup or connection error.
tests/ui/test_books_ui.py:39 and tests/ui/test_login_ui.py:37: both failing tests call BooksPage(...).open() as their first step, so the timeout happens before any assertion.
causes.suggested_fix: First, check the CI job environment for BUGS=slow_list (the workflow file .github/workflows/tests.yml does not set it, so it is inherited from elsewhere). If the slow path is not meant to be on in CI, unset it. If it is intended as a seeded flake for triage practice, the app's delay has to be bounded below the test budget or the test budget raised: for example, make the delay configurable and keep CI at 0, or raise the goto timeout for /books above 8 s (e.g., page.goto with timeout=15000 in tests/support/pages.py:34 only). Do not just retry-mask the failure without addressing the delay. Consider also asserting on a readiness element rather than the 'load' event so the test is not tied to the server's render time.
